analysis: The closest plan includes all seven UCR law courses, from foundations and rights through private, criminal, constitutional, public international and EU law. Ethics, negotiation, argument, social science and economics support how the law works in society. The public plan shifts five courses toward modern and imperial history, social theory, environmental movements and comparative policy analysis, with substantive weight on public institutions across legal systems. It offers EU, constitutional and international law and historical and policy inquiry; it does not substitute for Dutch administrative procedure, public enforcement or a legal clinic. The commercial plan adds transnational business law and keeps private and EU law, with finance, accounting, international trade and organizational study. AI ethics supplies privacy, fairness and accountability within the digital strand, without being a technology-law survey. Across the plans, empirical and historical research methods complement legal interpretation; legal drafting, Dutch procedural doctrine, supervised clinic work and courtroom advocacy remain materially different. The six positive alignments reflect shared areas of legal subject matter, and the other cells distinguish complements from counterparts.
